name: Law-enforcement equipment
source: Identifiers checked 2026-10-31 against the IEEE MA-L (OUI) registry and the Bluetooth SIG assigned numbers (company identifiers, 16-bit member UUIDs) bundled with RFWatch. Name/SSID patterns are community-reported. These are vendor/device signatures, not proof of police presence: the same vendors also sell to security firms, fleets, utilities and emergency services.

rules.label: Axon / TASER (body camera, Signal, TASER)
rules.note: OUI 00:25:DF (Axon Enterprise), Bluetooth SIG company 0x034D (TASER International; 0xFC81 also accepted in the company-ID field as seen live) and member UUIDs 0xFC81 (Axon Enterprise) / 0xFE6B, 0xFE6C (TASER International). Axon body cameras, Signal Sidearm/Vehicle triggers and TASER devices; vendor-level evidence only.

rules.label: WatchGuard Video (in-car / body camera)
rules.note: OUI 00:1D:96 is WatchGuard Video (police in-car and body cameras, now Motorola Solutions). Not WatchGuard Technologies (firewalls, 00:01:21 / 00:90:7F), which is deliberately excluded.

rules.label: Digital Ally (in-car / body camera)
rules.note: OUI 00:23:BD (Digital Ally, Inc.) — law-enforcement video systems.

rules.label: Utility Inc (police body / in-car video)
rules.note: OUIs 00:09:BC, 00:16:ED (Utility, Inc) — BodyWorn cameras and in-vehicle video/routers for police.

rules.label: Motorola Solutions (radio / body camera)
rules.note: Motorola Solutions OUIs, SIG company 0x04EC and member UUIDs 0xFD8E / 0xFE04: APX / MOTOTRBO radios, V300/VB400/Si500 body cameras, LEX handhelds. Used by AU police and emergency services but also by security and commercial radio users. Distinct from Motorola Mobility (consumer phones), which is excluded.

rules.label: Tait radio
rules.note: OUI 00:0D:CA (Tait Electronics) and SIG company 0x088F (Tait International). Tait radios are fielded by Australian/NZ police and emergency services, and by utilities.

rules.label: Public-safety radio / dispatch (Harris / Sepura / Hytera / Zetron)
rules.note: Harris Corporation, Sepura (TETRA) and Hytera OUIs. Radios with Wi-Fi/BLE programming interfaces; also sold commercially. Harris Government Communications (00:02:68) and Zetron dispatch (00:0B:13) added in v3.

rules.label: ALPR / plate-reader camera
rules.note: Flock Safety (B4:1E:52), Genetec AutoVu (00:0A:B1, 00:BF:15, 0C:BF:15), Elsag/Leonardo (00:40:DE, 00:80:E7) and Neology (00:17:3D) OUIs; Flock SSID/BLE names as reported by the Flock You project. Usually fixed roadside or vehicle-mounted cameras.

rules.label: Agency vehicle router / modem
rules.note: Cradlepoint (00:30:44, 00:E0:1C) and Sierra Wireless AirLink (00:A0:D5, 28:A3:31, 50:13:9D, 64:CE:6E, 84:DB:2F, CC:93:4A) in-vehicle routers, and Havis (00:1F:9C) vehicle docking. Standard uplinks in police cars, but also in ambulances, buses and utility fleets. v3 adds Peplink / Pepwave (MAX in-vehicle routers) OUIs — also used by buses and event networks.

rules.label: Rugged / forensic agency equipment
rules.note: Cellebrite (00:16:00) and i-PRO (D4:2D:C5, Panasonic Arbitrator in-car/body video) OUIs; Getac (rugged laptops and Getac Video body cameras) by name only.

rules.label: Police speed radar / lidar
rules.note: Decatur Electronics OUI 6C:18:11 (Genesis handheld/vehicle radar with Bluetooth printers/apps); other speed-enforcement vendors (Stalker/Applied Concepts, Kustom Signals, LTI, MPH, DragonEye) by name only — not in the IEEE/SIG registries.

rules.label: Rugged in-car computer (Toughbook / Getac)
rules.note: Panasonic Connect OUIs (Toughbook rugged laptops/tablets — the common police mobile data terminal; also utilities and field services).

rules.label: Emergency lighting / siren controller
rules.note: Emergency-vehicle lightbar/siren control brands, by advertised name only (not registered in IEEE/SIG). Also used by ambulances, fire and tow vehicles.

rules.label: Public-safety drone (Skydio)
rules.note: Skydio Inc. OUI 38:1D:14. Skydio X2/X10 are widely used in police drone-as-first-responder programs; also sold to enterprises.
